SPECTRA-based detection of drug-induced hepatotoxicity through extracellular vesicle analysis
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EV) are becoming crucial targets in liquid biopsy, diagnostics, and therapeutic applications, yet their nanoscale characterization remains challenging. In this context, the detection of drug-induced liver injury, i.e., hepatotoxicity, through EV molecular content remains unexplored. To this end, we present the SPECTRA - S urface P lasmonic E nhancement with C ombined T ransformative RA man and Interferometric Microscopy approach, which provides rapid, label-free EV content analysis under 30 minutes and requires only 1.3 microliters of sample. Using hepatic cultures as a model, our platform captures distinct and reproducible EV molecular changes in response to acetaminophen-induced hepatotoxicity. Across independent culture sets, a Gaussian Process Regression model predicted Acetaminophen (APAP) dose with median absolute error of 1.50 mM and minimal bias (Bland-Altman bias ~0.03 mM); cross-validated RMSE was 3.145 mM. These findings establish EVs as dynamic reporters of cellular drug responses and demonstrate use of SPECTRA for EV detection of hepatotoxicity.

title: Machine learning-assisted electrochemical SERS for sensitive detection of multiple urinary proteins
abstract: In this study, we report the development and application of a plasmonic nanostructure-based surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) platform, integrated with electrochemical deposition and a convolutional neural network (CNN), for the sensitive and precise detection and quantification of kidney disease biomarkers in urine. A gold nanodimple (AuND) substrate was subjected to electrochemical deposition to produce a highly reproducible and sensitive SERS substrate for protein analysis. Evaluation of the performance of the platform through reproducibility tests and quantitative analysis of Cytochrome C protein demonstrated that it has a high sensitivity and a low detection limit of 8.2 pg/mL. The system was then applied to multiplexed analysis of three kidney disease-related proteins: albumin, transferrin (TrF), and immunoglobulin G (IgG). A combination of ANOVA-based feature selection and CNN classification models achieved high accuracy, with classification accuracies of 93.8% for albumin, 96.8% for TrF, and 96.8% for IgG. Subsequently, CNN-based regression models were utilized to quantify protein concentrations in urine samples, demonstrating robust performance with R 2 values of 0.9321 for albumin, 0.9848 for TrF, and 0.9957 for IgG. The method also exhibited excellent diagnostic feasibility, successfully detecting and quantifying target proteins in a urine matrix. The proposed platform thus offers a highly sensitive, reliable and non-invasive approach for early diagnosis of kidney diseases.

title: CNN-assisted multimodal biosensing of Staphylococcus aureus using a bimetallic MOF@MXene hybrid nanomaterial
Machine learning-assisted colorimetric and photothermal detection of α-defensin using a competitive aptamer-based lateral flow biosensor with carbon nanotube tags
abstract: α-Defensin is a critical biomarker for joint infections such as periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), yet its rapid and sensitive detection remains challenging with conventional methods like ELISA and HPLC. Herein, we present a machine learning-assisted colorimetric and photothermal lateral flow biosensor for the sensitive and specific α-defensin detection in human samples. The biosensor adopts a competitive aptamer-based recognition mechanism, utilizes carbon nanotubes as dual-functional labels for visual and photothermal readouts, and integrates a machine learning algorithm to enhance detection accuracy. Molecular docking simulations were performed to clarify the binding mechanism between aptamer and α-defensin, thereby guiding the rational design of complementary DNA sequences and optimizing the competitive recognition strategy. The optimized biosensor demonstrated a wide detection range (5–5000 ng mL-1), a low limit of detection (4.01 ng mL-1), and high specificity against common interferents in synovial fluid. It also exhibited good repeatability and stability, and successfully discriminated infected from non-infected clinical synovial fluid samples. This integrated platform offers a portable, reliable, and user-friendly tool for point-of-care testing of α-defensin, and holds significant potential for clinical diagnostic applications.

TDM-OA-ICOS optical sensor for ppb-level C2H4 and CH4 simultaneous detection in postharvest fruit
abstract: Accurate and real-time monitoring of volatile gases is important for understanding fruit ripening processes, optimizing storage conditions, and ensuring food quality during postharvest storage. Ethylene (C2H4) acts as a key phytohormone regulating fruit ripening, while Methane (CH4) can serve as an indicator of microbial activity and spoilage-related biochemical processes. In this work, a high-sensitivity gas sensor based on Time-Division Multiplexed Off-Axis Integrated Cavity Output Spectroscopy (TDM-OA-ICOS) was developed for the simultaneous detection of C2H4 and CH4. To improve signal quality under complex storage environments, the demodulated 2f signals were processed using the Improved Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (ICEEMDAN) algorithm to effectively suppress noise and reduce mode mixing. Furthermore, an optimized concentration inversion model combining the Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm (SBOA) with the Least Squares Support Vector Machine (LSSVM) was established to enhance the accuracy of gas concentration retrieval. The sensor exhibited excellent linear responses for both gases, with limits of detection of 4.43 ppb for C2H4 and 1.19 ppb for CH4, as determined by Allan variance analysis. These results indicate that the proposed TDM-OA-ICOS sensor provides strong potential for applications in postharvest quality assessment, controlled-atmosphere storage, fermentation process monitoring, and food spoilage diagnostics.

Unlocking practical calibration of sensor arrays for environmental applications through a hybrid physical and machine learning model approach
abstract: Ion-selective electrode (ISE) arrays have proven useful in medical and other applications, but their use for measurement of environmental waters has lagged. Data-driven (machine learning) models are necessary to recover usable information from ISE arrays as physical models are not generally invertible, however curating training datasets can be prohibitively expensive. This work poses the question: to what extent might well-vetted physical models of the sensors be leveraged to augment training of data-driven models, therein unlocking broader application of ISE-based sensor arrays? Using a 10-element ISE array responsive to the majority of surface water charge balance and N-nutrient ions, environmentally-representative training samples (n=273) were measured. An extended Nikolsky-Eisenman model was created (residual RMSE 1–20 mV per sensor/target ion) and used to generate significantly more synthetic data (n > 10,000) than collected experimentally. Non-linear machine learning (ML) models (random forests, support vector regression, artificial neural networks, symbolic regression, deep neural networks) were trained to estimate target ion concentration (potassium, ammonium, and nitrate) as a function of varying proportions of experimental and synthetic data and increasing dataset size. The value-add of the sensor array approach increased as target ISE membrane selectivity worsened while augmenting experimental data with physically simulated synthetic data (up to 50% of total training dataset) improved quality of machine learning models for ion targets lacking highly selective membranes. This suggests that for challenging ion targets in complex mixed samples embedding physical laws into the ML training has the potential to support accelerated ISE array development with less overall experimental lab work required.

Label-free SERS fingerprint recognition of salivary biomarkers for Parkinson’s disease using hierarchical silver nanogrooves and transfer learning
abstract: Non-invasive identification of neuroprotein biomarkers in complex biofluids using surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) remains challenging. To address this, we developed a hierarchical silver nanogroove SERS substrate combined with a transfer learning strategy for salivary neuroprotein analysis. The hierarchical nanosurface features nanogrooves decorated with nanosynapses, which multilevel architecture enables the confinement of neuroprotein biomarkers within the multidimensional ”hotspots” regions of its nanoscale cavities. Hierarchical silver nanogrooves enabled label-free SERS fingerprint recognition of key neuroprotein biomarkers, such as Aβ, Tau, α-Synuclein and their mixtures. Then, a transfer learning model, trained solely on pure SERS spectra of these three proteins, extracts molecular fingerprints without requiring large mixed-analyte datasets. And the pretrained model was applied to identify α-Synuclein signals in saliva samples from 40 Parkinson’s disease (PD) patients, enabling non-invasive detection without retraining, achieving a high detection probability of 0.9678. In binary and ternary mixtures of α-Synuclein, Aβ, and Tau, the transfer learning program specifically identified the target protein. All probabilities exceeded the classification threshold, demonstrating consistent recognition of α-Synuclein-specific signatures despite complex protein backgrounds and saliva matrices. In sum, a non-invasive, label-free SERS detection of neuroproteins for neurodegenerative diseases using a transfer learning-enhanced hierarchical silver nanogroove platform is presented, this approach offers a promising pathway to facilitate clinical translation of SERS technology and support the diagnosis of neurodegenerative diseases, such as PD.

Strain-engineered active site migration and machine learning-assisted NO2 recognition in UV-activated Cs-doped WO3-x nanosheets with operando mechanistic insights
abstract: Pristine metal oxide gas sensors often suffer from poor selectivity and limited polarizability. To overcome these bottlenecks, oxygen vacancy-rich 2D ultrathin Cs-doped WO3-x nanosheets were synthesized via a solvothermal method. Advanced characterizations (KPFM, UPS, and TAS) confirmed that optimal Cs doping (0.08 mol%) optimizes the surface work function and drastically prolongs the photo-generated carrier lifetime (τ_3 = 40.45 ns), maximizing UV-excited charge separation. Consequently, under 365 nm UV illumination at 175℃, the sensor exhibited an ultra-high response of 118.4 to 10 ppm NO2, a 2.41 ppb limit of detection, ultra-fast kinetics (10 s/7 s response/recovery), superior immunity to moisture interference (stable across a 30% to 90% RH gradient), and robust 30-day long-term stability. To resolve cross-selectivity limitations, a machine learning model integrating Random Forest (RF) feature extraction and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) was deployed, achieving 98.8% recognition accuracy in multi-component gas mixtures. Mechanistically, in-situ/operando Raman Two-Dimensional Correlation Spectroscopy (2D-COS) and Density Functional Theory (DFT) revealed that steric hindrance from large Cs+ ions induces localized W-O lattice strain while effectively eliminating surface moisture side reactions. This strain creates distorted sites with ultra-high adsorption energy (-1.3538 eV), driving a ”complete migration” of NO2 active adsorption sites away from the intrinsic lattice. By coupling strain-engineered active site migration with artificial intelligence, this work provides a powerful blueprint for the next generation of highly selective, intelligent gas sensors.

title: Machine learning-assisted multi-emission Tb/Eu-MOF fluorescence array for ligand discrimination and quantification of silver nanoparticles released from textiles
Differential competitive mechanism-driven three-channel sensor array for machine learning-enabled organophosphorus pesticides identification
abstract: The rapid and accurate identification of organophosphorus pesticides (OPs) is crucial for ensuring food safety. However, the discrimination of structurally similar pesticide analogues across varying concentrations remains a formidable challenge. In this work, a three-channel sensor array integrating dual-colorimetric and photothermal responses was developed using performance-optimized Au/MIL-100(Fe) nanozyme as recognition unit for the precise detection and intelligent discrimination of OPs. Mechanistic studies revealed that OPs inhibit catalytic activity by binding to the active centers of the nanozymes through coordination, thereby generating distinct signal patterns. Based on this response feature, a concentration-independent recognition model was established using artificial neural networks (ANN), achieving nearly 100% accurate identification of five types of OPs. The sensor array reached a picomolar (pM) limit of detection, and maintained excellent anti-interference capability and stability in complex matrices (tap water, cabbage, and peaches), offering a versatile tool for high-throughput, intelligent pesticide residue screening.
